name: Sodium-ion batteries
summary: Rechargeable batteries use sodium ions as the charge carrier, offering another chemistry for selected transport and stationary applications.
useCase: A low-cost or cold-climate vehicle uses sodium-ion cells where energy density is sufficient and temperature performance or material supply is valuable.
whyNow: CATL has advanced from a first-generation announcement to later cells and a passenger-vehicle unveiling. Commercial competitiveness still depends on cost and production yield relative to continually improving lithium iron phosphate.

mainstream.scope: Routine use in selected budget or cold-weather vehicles and stationary storage products; not wholesale replacement of lithium-ion.
mainstream.rationale: Major manufacturers and initial vehicle programmes support a plausible commercial pathway. Lower energy density and cheap competing LFP can delay adoption. Manufacturer mass-production language should be checked against actual shipped GWh.

metric.name: CATL announced sodium-ion cell energy density
metric.scope: Manufacturer specifications for successive cell generations; performance proxy
metric.limitations: Company-announced cell specifications, not independent like-for-like pack tests, installed GWh or market share. The 2026 figure accompanies a vehicle unveiling; it does not establish production volume. Pack-level density will be lower.
metric.futureNote: Separate forward signals show a 1 GWh end-2026 company shipment target and a 60 GWh three-year supply agreement. Neither can be plotted as an extension of cell energy density.
metric.growthLabel: +15 Wh/kg in stated CATL cell density since 2021; no inferred shipment growth.

milestones.text: CATL’s first-generation sodium-ion announcement reported up to 160 Wh/kg.
No comparable commercial shipment measurement is included for 2022.
No comparable annual shipment measurement is included for 2023.
No comparable annual shipment measurement is included for 2024; no production total is inferred from product demonstrations.
CATL launched Naxtra with a stated 175 Wh/kg cell specification.

CATL and Changan unveiled a sodium-ion passenger vehicle in February. CATL later announced a 60 GWh three-year storage supply agreement and a 1 GWh end-2026 shipment target; neither is an observed annual shipment total.

tailwinds: Sodium provides a different raw-material supply chain
Cold-temperature performance can create specific use cases
Multiple battery suppliers can adapt existing manufacturing expertise
bottlenecks: Energy density is lower than leading lithium-ion cells
LFP price declines can remove the expected cost advantage
Hard-carbon supply, yield and customer qualification
watchMetrics: Commercially shipped GWh and delivered vehicles
Pack cost per kWh versus LFP at comparable scale
Cycle life, cold performance and warranty claims in actual use
